summary: Qian Cao is an Indology and philosophy scholar. Cao studied as a PhD student at Ghent University and also held a faculty post there (both attested 2026).

Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Lin studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol (MA, 2004), and the University of Washington (PhD, attested 2015) under Collett Cox, later holding a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2026).

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Hung Wu and Irene Winter and earned masters degrees from UCAS and Warwick. Ning held teaching posts at Michigan, Yale, and San Diego State, and researched at Dunhuang Academy.

Qichao Liang (1873–1929) was a sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Xuehai Tang, National Tsing Hua University, and under Youwei Kang. Liang held posts at the Current Affairs Academy, the Translation Bureau, Nankai University, Tsinghua University, and the National Library of China.

Qing Duan (1953–2022) specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University and earning a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ronald Eric Emmerick, Duan served as a professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

Qingying Chen (1942–2022) was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Qinghai Nationalities University, Qinghai Normal University, and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao. Chen worked at Delingha High School, Qinghai Nationalities University, Minzu University, and the China Tibetology Research Center.

Qingzhi Zhu specializes in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and sinology. After studying at Northwest Normal University, Central China Normal University, and Sichuan University, Zhu held professorial appointments at Peking University (1998–2014) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Qiwen Xiao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

Quentin Devers is a history, archaeology, and Tibetology researcher. Devers worked as a research assistant at the University of Virginia (2008–2010), an archaeologist at Heritage WA (2012), and became a charg�e9 de recherche at CNRS in 2016.
R. Balasubramanian (1929–2017) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras (~1976–1989).

R. D. Vadekar (1902–1986) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shripad Krishna Belvalkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Allied Languages at Fergusson College (attested 1958).
R. Gayathri is an Indology scholar who studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) worked in religious studies and Indology after studying at Columbia and the LSE. He held positions in journalism, served in the AEF and the ACLS, and worked at Guaranty Trust Company and J.P. Morgan & Co.

R. H. Blyth (1898–1964) was a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Ilford County High School and the University of London, he later held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1925–1940) and Kanazawa University.

R. H. Tawney (1880–1962) was a historian educated at Rugby School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1908) and the London School of Economics (~1913–1949).

R. K. Bodhe is an Indology scholar who studied at the R.C. Patel Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (2017–2019) and served as a Research Officer at Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005).
R. Keller Kimbrough is a Japanology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD from Yale University and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2013).
R. N. Gadre is an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Sir Parashurambhau College and at Savitribai Phule Pune University (both attested 1958).
R. P. Paranjpye (1876–1966) studied under Vaman Shivram Apte and served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).
